documents.title: Site Progress Report – Berth 7-9 Modernization
documents.content:
**3.3 Berth 9 – Dredging and Pocket Works**

Dredging of the berth 9 pocket continued with MDP-2 working extended hours to offset the downtime of MDP-1. A total of 4,850 m³ of material was removed during the week, against a planned 5,200 m³. The shortfall is attributed to the single dredger operation and is expected to be recovered once MDP-1 returns to service. Survey of the pocket indicates an average depth of –13.8 m CD, still 0.4 m above the required –14.2 m CD. Dredging will continue for the next two weeks before re-survey.

**3.4 Berth 7-9 – Utility Relocation and Services**

Cable duct installation along the berth 7 service corridor was completed. A total of 320 m of ducting was laid, and pull wires were installed. The remaining connection to the existing substation at chainage 7+050 is pending approval from the NDPA electrical department. The approval request was submitted on 18 May; no response has been received as of the date of this report.

Water supply line relocation at berth 8 was completed and pressure tested on 21 May. The test was successful at 6 bar for 30 minutes with no visible leaks. The old line has been capped and will be abandoned in place.

**3.5 Berth 7 – Crane Rail and Deck Repairs**

Grinding and welding of the crane rail joint at chainage 7+400 was completed. The joint was re-surveyed and found to be within tolerance. A second joint at chainage 7+460 was identified as showing wear and has been marked for repair next week. The repair will require a short shutdown of the rail section, which has been coordinated with the terminal operator.

Deck spalling repairs continued along the berth 7 apron. A total of 18 m² of spalled concrete was removed and reinstated. The repaired areas have been cured and will be tested for integrity using a Schmidt hammer next week.

**4.0 SAFETY**

One minor incident was recorded this week. On 21 May, a worker sustained a small cut to his hand while handling steel reinforcement at berth 8. The worker was treated at the site clinic and returned to duty the same day. The incident has been recorded in the site safety register and will be included in the monthly safety statistics.

Toolbox talks were conducted on the following topics:
- Lifting operations and hand signals (20 May)
- Working near water and personal flotation devices (21 May)
- Manual handling and ergonomics (22 May)

No lost-time injuries were recorded during the week.

**5.0 QUALITY CONTROL**

Concrete cube results for pours conducted during the week of 12 May were received. All cubes passed the required 28-day compressive strength of 30 N/mm². The results are attached to this report as Appendix Q-14.

Pile driving records for the week were reviewed by the quality team. All piles driven were within the specified verticality tolerance of 1:100. Pile driving records are available for inspection at the site office.
